newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil stock correction seen persisting.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil stock correction seen persisting.

text.p: A winter chill blanketing Canadian energy company stocks is expected to persist at least though spring as investors grow more jittery over weakening oil and natural gas prices.
"Are we in a correction? Yes. Do I think the correction's over? No," Wilf Gobert, managing director of research for brokerage Peters & Co., said on Tuesday.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas index, which includes the stocks of producers and integrated energy companies, has lost more than 10 percent in the past month, dropping to 6,232 points on Monday from an all-time high of 6,960 on Jan. 20. The index was up about 60 points to 6,292 on Tuesday.

The selloff in energy companies, which had enjoyed a bull run in Canada for well over a year, came despite booming drilling activity in the sector and the February flood of cash into the stock market as Canadians rushed to meet the annual deadline for investing retirement funds.

"It's pretty apparent that the commodity price is what triggered the the whole turn in momentum and now people are looking for the trigger that's going to change the momentum from negative to positive," said Matt Janisch, analyst with Nesbitt Burns in Calgary.

Prices for benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude oil on the New York Mercantile Exchange have recently hovered just above $20 a barrel after reaching a post-Gulf War high late last year of almost $27.
The drop has been driven by a warmer than expected winter, which erased fears of heating oil shortages, and a belief by some market watchers that the world was awash in crude.

NYMEX natural gas prices have meanwhile skidded below $2 per million British thermal units after averaging about $4 in December and January. Canadian gas prices, while expected to average higher levels than last year, have also weakened since November and December.
"You can't say with any certainty that oil and natural gas prices won't go lower and therefore the assumptions that underpin the financial projections are what have come into question," Gobert said.
Peter Linder, analyst with brokerage CIBC Wood Gundy, said his general bearishness on Canadian oil stocks led him this week to pull previous "buy" recommendations from 15 of the 26 firms he follows.
"I saw oil and gas prices coming off fairly significantly and I didn't see much upside in the next three to six months," Linder said. "If anything, I saw further weakness."
He also said first-half production growth for many companies was likely to be under analysts' targets because of a shortage of available drilling rigs in Canada this winter.
But the winter cooling of stock prices in the sector presented some buying opportunities, analysts said.
Linder said Canadian Natural Resources Ltd., whose share price rose to a high of almost C$40 in January, represented good value at its current C$33.75 level.
Pan East Petroleum Corp., known for exploration of large natural gas reserves in northern Alberta, was his top pick among small producers.

Gobert said Newport Petroleum Corp., whose stock price has dropped about 30 percent over investor fears that it may be paying too much to take over Cimarron Petroleum Ltd., appeared undervalued at C$7.45.
He also said his firm was recommending oilfield services and drilling stocks, as the Canadian industry maintained its record winter drilling pace.
